title: The Rewind: Us and Them
summary:
One of the most significant ways in which these differences manifest themselves is in terms of
attitude toward risk. If you're confident that you know what the future holds,
risk isn't frightening. Our kind of investor is preoccupied by risk, whereas I think the
other is often oblivious to it.

thesis: Howard Marks argues that the investment community is divided into two distinct groups: the 'I know' school, which holds dangerous confidence exceeding its merits, and the 'I don't know' school, which acknowledges uncertainty. He asserts that the most dangerous attitude in investing is being 100% certain about outcomes, noting that his own long-term consistency and lack of embarrassing losses stem from a defensive approach rather than claiming to know the market's movements.
